opinion: a personal view or belief about something, not necessarily based on fact
Everyone in the meeting had a different opinion about the plan.
article: a piece of writing published in a newspaper or magazine
She wrote an article about renewable energy for the local paper.
wrote: The list turns out to be the part nobody ever wrote down.
these: used to refer to people or things nearby or just mentioned
These shoes are far more comfortable than my old ones.
grounds: reasons or justifications for a belief or action
The decision was criticised on legal and ethical grounds.
alone: without other people or things present
He prefers to travel alone rather than join a large tour group.
pipe: a tube through which liquid or gas flows
Water leaked slowly from a cracked pipe under the kitchen sink.
dream: a series of thoughts during sleep, or a strong hope or ambition
Owning her own bakery had always been her lifelong dream.
impossible: not able to happen or be done
It seemed impossible to finish the project in one week.
intellectuals: people who value and engage seriously in study and ideas
Many intellectuals gathered to debate the country's new education policy.
demanding: requiring a lot of skill, effort, or attention
Nursing is a demanding job that requires both patience and stamina.
introduction: the opening section of a text, or the act of bringing something in
The book's introduction explains why the author chose this topic.
involving: including or concerning something as a necessary part
Police reported a crash involving three vehicles on the highway.
could: past tense of can, used to express ability or possibility
She could speak three languages fluently by the age of ten.
further: to a greater extent or distance; additionally
They walked further into the forest to find the waterfall.
delay: a period of time when something happens later than planned
The flight was cancelled after a long delay at the gate.
goal: an aim or desired result that someone works towards
Her main goal this year is to save enough money to travel.
13-year-old: A 13-year-old boy won the regional science competition last month.
student: a person who is studying at a school, college or university
Every student in the class handed in their essay on time.
barry: a surname used as a proper name
Barry is a common surname across several West African countries.
seems: gives the impression of being something
It seems likely that prices will keep rising this year.
far: to a great extent; at or to a great distance
This plan works far better than the last one did.
removed: The stubborn stain was finally removed with a strong cleaner.
such: of the type already mentioned or described
Such behaviour will not be tolerated in the workplace.
debates: formal or informal discussions in which people argue different views
Similar debates about screen time occur in classrooms worldwide.
can't: contraction of 'cannot', expressing inability or impossibility
I can't attend the meeting because I'll be travelling that day.
wait: to stay in a place or delay action until something happens
The baker's real skill lies in knowing when to wait and when to stop.
study: a piece of research carried out to examine a subject in detail
A new study links poor sleep to a weaker immune system.
sixth: coming after fifth in a sequence; number 6 in order
My daughter just started sixth grade at her new school.
grade: a mark or score given to indicate quality or achievement
He worked hard all semester to improve his final grade.
